channel.title: PFS Filters Guides & Resources
channel.description: Paint booth filter selection, maintenance, and compliance guidance from PFS Filters.

item.title: How Often Should You Change Paint Booth Filters?
item.description: There is no universal replacement interval. Use booth and filter manufacturer limits, filter-stage inspections, pressure readings, operating conditions, and documented trends to set a defensible schedule.

item.title: Fiberglass vs. Tacky Panel Filters
item.description: Fiberglass paint arrestors and tackified panel media are not automatically interchangeable. Compare the documented filter stage, dimensions, media, airflow direction, and equipment requirements before ordering.

item.title: Paint Booth Filter Maintenance Checklist
item.description: Use this general checklist to organize filter inspections and records, then apply the spray booth manual, filter instructions, permit conditions, and facility procedures that control your installation.

item.title: EPA Method 319 for Aerospace Paint Booth Filters
item.description: EPA Method 319 is a test method for determining paint overspray arrestor filtration efficiency. It is not a blanket certification for every installation, coating, operating condition, or facility obligation.

item.title: How Often to Change Booth Filters
item.description: Exhaust filters are typically changed every 30 to 90 days, and intake filters every 3 to 6 months. Life depends on spray hours, coatings, and pressure.

item.title: What Clogged Booth Filters Do
item.description: Clogged booth filters cut airflow. Face velocity can drop below the NFPA 33 minimum of 100 feet per minute. Change the loaded stage before you keep spraying.

item.title: How to Choose Booth Filters
item.description: Choose booth filters by stage, measured opening, and media family. Powder, carbon, and PFS booth kits are quoted when the catalog has no matching product.

item.title: Booth Filter Maintenance Checklist
item.description: Booth filter maintenance checklist: daily floor and gauge checks, weekly light and seal inspections, and when to change exhaust or intake media.
